privacy: sanitized; no tokens, installation IDs, private repository names, private conversation text, or raw connector payloads

observations.fact: Native OpenAI GitHub connector could read repository state but write attempts returned 403 Resource not accessible by integration.
observations.control: A separately authenticated governed GitHub CLI route could write and read back the same user-owned repositories.

observations.fact: After revoke/reinstall/reconnect with all-repository read/write access, the native connector resolved the authenticated account and returned the user's admin collaborator role on a user-owned repository. That role does not establish the connector token or GitHub App effective scopes.
The first harmless native write path did not reach a stable postcondition because the connector became unavailable/disabled rather than returning the earlier stable 403 class.
observations.control: Governed GitHub CLI access remained usable against the same account/repository state.

observations.fact: Native source search and a later branch-creation attempt each caused the connector to become unavailable in separate bounded probes.

The native connector was rediscovered with issue/PR read schemas, then became disabled on an independent readback attempt. Exact remote SHA and PR state remained readable through a separate governed GitHub route.

inference: Observed behavior is consistent with runtime/session-scoped connector or tool-registry instability, but it does not rule out a static connector or GitHub App permission limitation. The governed CLI control demonstrates repository reachability through separate credentials, not native connector token authority.
unknown: Effective scopes/permissions of the native connector token or GitHub App at the failing operations.
Whether tool loss is caused by MCP/tool registry refresh, GitHub App installation state propagation, connector authorization cache invalidation, or another platform layer.
Whether the triggering operation matters or only exposes an already-stale connector state.
Whether failure scope is chat/thread/runtime-specific or shared across concurrent sessions.
